name: Curacao
rule: Curaçao customs requires permits for plants and flowers but does not classify manufactured dried tea. Personal goods customs clearance alone is insufficient agricultural evidence.

2026-09-30: Current Warenlandsverordening article 2(1) likewise excludes manufacture within a private household, not import of purchased retail food. Article3(1)(j)–(k) authorizes import/export and registration rules, not a self-executing universal origin certificate; regulation-making powers alone do not exclude personal tea. The publicly indexed permit-list decree concerns specific bakery/meat/produce categories, not a new tea ruling. No material personal-postal exemption/barrier established; LVV finished-tea conditions remain missing.

2026-09-30 fresh official online recovery: Recovered the current-linked Dutch NPPO diverse-product Curaçao sheet, effective 22 May 2013, and the Curaçao Fair Trade Authority 2024 food-market report. The NPPO sheet has no populated certificate commodity list and states no specific requirements are known; it says a requested certificate for an unnamed product requires official destination information and assessment. Its missing-information statement is not a positive Curaçao permit/certificate exemption for Japanese tea. The local authority report maps food import laws but supplies no all-private-food certificate duty or manufactured-tea waiver. Saved full PDFs/texts cw-nvwa-diverse2013 and cw-ftac2024.

30 September renewed official-source/general-definition review: Recovered USDA’s official 23 December 2013 Curaçao FAIRS report (CB1317). It distinguishes processed products monitored at retail from plant products controlled at entry; it also says most processed products require a free-sale certificate and product samples sent by parcel post are subject only to customs duty. Neither statement settles the current private paid 100 g order: the report is old, written for US commercial exporters, supplies no exact enacted certificate provision or personal-use scope, and a purchase is not a trade sample. Native-language official legal searches returned pesticide/CITES/tariff provisions rather than a new operative manufactured-tea plant rule. No conclusion was drawn from unrelated EU plant rules.
